ambiguities.evidence: The preliminaries call c_1 and c_2 functions of n, A, r̂_i, and u_s, while Theorem 4.1 states one condition c_1κ∞(A)u_s<1 and then concludes the recurrence for every i≥0. [PDF pp. 5 and 9, printed A821 and A825, solver-model explanation and Theorem 4.1]
ambiguities.impact: If c_1 and c_2 vary with i, the solver bound and strict denominator condition must be read pointwise for every iteration, and α_i inherits that dependence; treating them as global constants requires an additional uniformity assumption. [PDF pp. 5 and 9, printed A821 and A825, equation (2.4) and Theorem 4.1]
ambiguities.issue: The theorem writes c_1 and c_2 without iteration subscripts even though the preliminaries allow them to depend on r̂_i. [PDF pp. 5 and 9, printed A821 and A825, text after equations (2.3)-(2.5) and Theorem 4.1]

ambiguities.evidence: γ_p^r is defined with denominator 1−pu_r, but the theorem explicitly states only nonsingularity, (2.4), and c_1κ∞(A)u_s<1. [PDF pp. 5 and 9, printed A821 and A825, definition of γ_k and Theorem 4.1]
ambiguities.impact: A fully explicit formal statement must either assume pu_r<1 or bind γ_p^r abstractly together with the residual-error premise. [PDF pp. 5 and 7, printed A821 and A823, definition of γ_p^r and equation (3.3)]
ambiguities.issue: The standard-model smallness requirement needed for finite γ_p^r is implicit rather than included among Theorem 4.1's explicit hypotheses. [PDF pp. 5, 7, and 9, printed A821, A823, and A825, definition of γ_k, equation (3.3), and Theorem 4.1]

contract_plain_english: If every correction solve has the normwise residual quality prescribed by (2.4) and c_1κ∞(A)u_s is below one, then one refinement step satisfies an explicit infinity-norm residual recurrence. Its multiplicative coefficient contains the correction-solver instability, while its additive term contains residual-computation and update-rounding errors with all finite-precision factors retained. [PDF pp. 8-9, printed A824-A825, equation (4.1), displayed derivation, and Theorem 4.1]

source_evidence.observation: The theorem concerns the computed iterates of the unscaled mixed-precision iterative-refinement algorithm.
The paper defines κ∞(A)=‖A^{-1}‖∞‖A‖∞ and assumes a normwise correction-solver residual bound involving nonnegative quantities c_1 and c_2.
The residual-computation and update-rounding errors have the componentwise models later converted to infinity-norm bounds.
After defining h_i=r̂_i−A d̂_i, the paper applies (2.4) and bounds d̂_i through A^{-1}(r̂_i−h_i).

source_evidence.anchor: displayed derivation immediately before Theorem 4.1 and Theorem 4.1
source_evidence.observation: Under c_1κ∞(A)u_s<1, the correction defect is isolated and then substituted into (4.1), yielding the residual recurrence and the exact displayed definitions of α_i and β_i.
The analysis ignores underflow and overflow; scaling is proposed later as a modified algorithm.

statement.algorithm_linkage: The result bounds one unscaled Algorithm 1.1 step by combining the residual rounding model, the normwise correction-solver defect model (2.4), and the precision-u update model. [PDF pp. 2, 7-9, printed A818 and A823-A825, Algorithm 1.1, equations (2.4), (3.3), (3.6), (4.1), and Theorem 4.1]
binders: Let A ∈ ℝ^{n×n} be nonsingular and b ∈ ℝ^n, and let Algorithm 1.1 produce x̂_i, r̂_i, d̂_i, and x̂_{i+1} for i ≥ 0. [PDF pp. 2 and 9, printed A818 and A825, Algorithm 1.1 and Theorem 4.1]
Let c_1 and c_2 be the nonnegative solver-bound quantities from (2.4), and define h_i := r̂_i−A d̂_i. [PDF pp. 5 and 8, printed A821 and A824, equation (2.4) and the text after (4.1)]

Let κ∞(A):=‖A^{-1}‖∞‖A‖∞, let p be the maximum row nonzero count of [A b], and let γ_p^r:=pu_r/(1−pu_r). [PDF pp. 5 and 7, printed A821 and A823, equation (2.1), definition of γ_k, and text preceding (3.3)]
conclusions: The exact starting identity is A x̂_{i+1}−b=Δr_i+A d̂_i−r̂_i+AΔx_i. [PDF p. 8, printed A824, equation (4.1)]
The first correction-defect bound is ‖h_i‖∞ ≤ u_s(c_1‖A‖∞‖d̂_i‖∞+c_2‖r̂_i‖∞) ≤ u_s(c_1‖A‖∞‖A^{-1}‖∞(‖r̂_i‖∞+‖h_i‖∞)+c_2‖r̂_i‖∞). [PDF p. 8, printed A824, displayed h_i derivation]
Isolating h_i under c_1κ∞(A)u_s<1 gives ‖h_i‖∞ ≤ u_s[(c_1κ∞(A)+c_2)/(1−c_1κ∞(A)u_s)]‖r̂_i‖∞. [PDF p. 9, printed A825, first displayed bound]

Before eliminating r̂_i, the one-step residual bound is ‖b−Ax̂_{i+1}‖∞ ≤ u_s‖b−Ax̂_i‖∞+(1+u_s)γ_p^r(‖b‖∞+‖A‖∞‖x̂_i‖∞)+u_s[(c_1κ∞(A)+c_2)/(1−c_1κ∞(A)u_s)]‖r̂_i‖∞+u‖A‖∞‖x̂_{i+1}‖∞. [PDF p. 9, printed A825, first residual inequality before Theorem 4.1]
After a second use of (3.3), Theorem 4.1 concludes ‖b−Ax̂_{i+1}‖∞ ≤ α_i‖b−Ax̂_i‖∞+β_i for every i≥0. [PDF p. 9, printed A825, final displayed derivation and Theorem 4.1]
The coefficient is α_i=u_s(1+(1+u_s)(c_1κ∞(A)+c_2)/(1−c_1κ∞(A)u_s)). [PDF p. 9, printed A825, Theorem 4.1]
The additive term is β_i=(1+u_s(c_1κ∞(A)+c_2)/(1−c_1κ∞(A)u_s))(1+u_s)γ_p^r(‖b‖∞+‖A‖∞‖x̂_i‖∞)+u‖A‖∞‖x̂_{i+1}‖∞. [PDF p. 9, printed A825, Theorem 4.1]
constants_and_indexing: The result is quantified for i≥0 and relates residual i+1 to residual i. [PDF p. 9, printed A825, Theorem 4.1]
The strict condition is c_1κ∞(A)u_s<1, and the same expression appears in the exact denominator 1−c_1κ∞(A)u_s. [PDF p. 9, printed A825, defect bound and Theorem 4.1]
α_i contains the factor 1+u_s outside the correction-defect ratio, while β_i contains both 1+u_s and the separate update term involving x̂_{i+1}. [PDF p. 9, printed A825, Theorem 4.1]
The residual-rounding contribution in β_i uses x̂_i, whereas the update-rounding contribution uses x̂_{i+1}. [PDF p. 9, printed A825, Theorem 4.1]
definitions_and_conventions: h_i is the computed correction-equation residual r̂_i−A d̂_i, whereas b−Ax̂_i is the exact residual of the current stored iterate for the original system. [PDF pp. 8-9, printed A824-A825, text after (4.1) and Theorem 4.1]
c_1 and c_2 are nonnegative functions of n, A, r̂_i, and u_s according to the preliminary solver model. [PDF p. 5, printed A821, text following equations (2.3)-(2.5)]
γ_p^r=pu_r/(1−pu_r), with p the maximum number of nonzeros in a row of [A b]. [PDF pp. 5 and 7, printed A821 and A823, definition of γ_k and text preceding (3.3)]
error_notions: The recurrence controls the exact normwise residual ‖b−Ax̂_i‖∞ of the original system, not the computed residual norm ‖r̂_i‖∞. [PDF p. 9, printed A825, Theorem 4.1]
h_i measures the residual of the computed correction d̂_i in the correction equation A d=r̂_i. [PDF pp. 5 and 8, printed A821 and A824, equation (2.4) and definition of h_i]

Theorem 4.1 itself does not normalize the residual by ‖A‖∞‖x̂_i‖∞+‖b‖∞ and therefore does not by itself state a bound on the normwise relative backward error η. [PDF pp. 5 and 9, printed A821 and A825, definition of η and Theorem 4.1]
exceptional_values: The strict denominator condition excludes 1−c_1κ∞(A)u_s≤0. [PDF p. 9, printed A825, assumption preceding the isolated h_i bound and Theorem 4.1]

The γ_p^r expression presupposes a finite standard-model bound, ordinarily pu_r<1; this side condition is not restated in Theorem 4.1. [PDF pp. 5 and 7, printed A821 and A823, definition and use of γ_p^r]
Underflow and overflow are ignored by this analysis; the later scaling modification is outside Theorem 4.1 as stated. [PDF p. 12, printed A828, section 6, Scaling]
higher_order_terms: Theorem 4.1 is stated with exact rational factors in u_s and does not use big-O or ≲ notation. [PDF p. 9, printed A825, Theorem 4.1]
Factors 1+u_s and the denominator 1−c_1κ∞(A)u_s are retained and must not be silently replaced by first-order approximations. [PDF p. 9, printed A825, displayed derivation and Theorem 4.1]
hypotheses: The solver used in step 4 satisfies ‖r̂_i−A d̂_i‖∞ ≤ u_s(c_1‖A‖∞‖d̂_i‖∞+c_2‖r̂_i‖∞). [PDF p. 5, printed A821, equation (2.4)]
The denominator condition c_1κ∞(A)u_s<1 holds. [PDF p. 9, printed A825, opening line of the derivation and Theorem 4.1]
The residual and update obey r̂_i=b−Ax̂_i+Δr_i with the bound in (3.3), and x̂_{i+1}=x̂_i+d̂_i+Δx_i with |Δx_i|≤u|x̂_{i+1}|. [PDF p. 7, printed A823, equations (3.3) and (3.6)]
The unit roundoffs inherit u_r≤u≤u_s≤u_f from the algorithm's precision ordering. [PDF pp. 1-2, printed A817-A818, equation (1.1) and the definition of u_s]
implicit_context: A and b are precision-u input data, residuals are computed at u_r and rounded to u_s, corrections are effectively solved at u_s and stored at u, and updates are performed at u. [PDF pp. 1-2, printed A817-A818, precision definitions and Algorithm 1.1]

Theorem 4.1 requires only solver condition (2.4), not the relative-forward-solve condition (2.3) or componentwise solver condition (2.5). [PDF pp. 5 and 9, printed A821 and A825, equations (2.3)-(2.5) and Theorem 4.1]

Although labeled α_i, its displayed formula depends on i only through any iteration dependence hidden in c_1 and c_2; β_i additionally contains x̂_i and x̂_{i+1}. [PDF pp. 5 and 9, printed A821 and A825, text after equations (2.3)-(2.5) and Theorem 4.1]
norms: Every norm in the theorem and its displayed derivation is the vector or induced matrix infinity norm. [PDF pp. 8-9, printed A824-A825, h_i derivation and Theorem 4.1]
The passage uses κ∞(A), not a two-norm condition number or the componentwise condition number cond(A). [PDF pp. 5 and 9, printed A821 and A825, equation (2.1) and Theorem 4.1]
numerical_model: The standard floating-point model is used at unit roundoffs u_r, u_s, and u; u_f does not enter the recurrence explicitly. [PDF pp. 1-2, 5, and 9, printed A817-A818, A821, and A825, precision definitions, section 2 model, and Theorem 4.1]

Residual computation contributes the γ_p^r term and residual rounding contributes factors involving u_s; update rounding contributes u‖A‖∞‖x̂_{i+1}‖∞. [PDF pp. 7 and 9, printed A823 and A825, equations (3.3), (3.6), and Theorem 4.1]
The correction-solver model is a normwise residual/backward-error condition, not an exact-solve or relative-forward-error assumption. [PDF p. 5, printed A821, equation (2.4) and its explanation]

undebatable_constraints: A is a nonsingular real n×n matrix and the theorem concerns Algorithm 1.1 iterates for every i≥0. [PDF p. 9, printed A825, Theorem 4.1]
The required solver premise is exactly the normwise condition (2.4), together with c_1κ∞(A)u_s<1. [PDF pp. 5 and 9, printed A821 and A825, equation (2.4) and Theorem 4.1]
The contraction coefficient α_i is independent of u_r explicitly; u_r occurs through γ_p^r only in β_i. [PDF p. 9, printed A825, Theorem 4.1]
The theorem bounds the exact original-system residual in the infinity norm and makes no direct forward-error or componentwise-error claim. [PDF p. 9, printed A825, Theorem 4.1]
No factor, denominator, or i-to-i+1 offset in the displayed α_i and β_i formulas may be dropped. [PDF p. 9, printed A825, Theorem 4.1]
